questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The letter will be delivered by the postman tomorrow.
options_en: The postman delivered the letter tomorrow
The postman will have delivered the letter tomorrow.
The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow.
The postman will be delivering the letter tomorrow.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (3) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow."

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) For comprehensive understanding of complex subjects,

(b) and consistent review of material

(c) active participation in discussions,

(d) are absolutely essential for students

(e) diligent note-taking during lectures,
questions.solution_en:
(a) For comprehensive understanding of complex subjects, - This introductory prepositional phrase sets the context or purpose for what follows. It indicates why the subsequent actions are necessary.

(c) active participation in discussions, - This is the first item in a list of essential actions or requirements that form the compound subject of the sentence. It follows the introductory phrase: "For comprehensive understanding of complex subjects, active participation in discussions,"

(e) diligent note-taking during lectures, - This is the second item in the list of essential actions, parallel in structure to (c). It continues the enumeration: "...active participation in discussions, diligent note-taking during lectures,"

(b) and consistent review of material - This is the third and final item in the list, connected by the conjunction "and." It completes the compound subject: "...diligent note-taking during lectures, and consistent review of material"

(d) are absolutely essential for students - This is the predicate of the sentence, with "are" agreeing with the plural compound subject (participation, note-taking, and review), and "absolutely essential for students" explaining their importance.

Final sentence: "For comprehensive understanding of complex subjects, active participation in discussions, diligent note-taking during lectures, and consistent review of material are absolutely essential for students."

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

Shyam asked me how I had persuaded his sister.
options_en: "How are you persuading my sister?" Shyam asked me.
"How did you persuaded my sister?" Shyam asked me.
"How did you persuade my sister?" Shyam asked me.
"How have you persuade me sister?" Shyam asked me.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

· Tense remains same

· Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

· Past perfect changes to Simple Past

In these cases, we go by the options.

As per the given options, the given indirect from in past perfect tense is to be changed to the past simple tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

The reporting verb may remain the same or be changed to 'said'.

'How I had' is changed to 'how did you'

The pronoun 'his' is changed to 'my'.

'Did' is always followed by the base verb. So, option (b) is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): "How did you persuade my sister?" Shyam asked me.

questions.solution_en:
The word "paradox" doesn't accurately convey the intended meaning in the context of the sentence. A "paradox" is a concept or statement that seems contradictory or goes against common belief, yet it might be true or logical within a specific context. In contrast, the sentence implies that the speaker played a trick or a practical joke on his/her sister by hiding fake spiders in her room. This action aligns more with the concept of a "prank" rather than a "paradox." A prank involves a playful or mischievous act intended to trick, amuse, or surprise someone, typically in a light-hearted manner. Accordingly, 'prank' is a suitable word to replace 'paradox'. 'Foul' refers to something that is offensive, unpleasant, or morally unacceptable. However, in the context of the sentence, the act of hiding fake spiders as a joke on the sister doesn't necessarily imply anything offensive or morally wrong. Therefore, "foul" doesn't appropriately replace "paradox" in this context. A 'riddle' is a type of puzzle or enigmatic question that requires thought or cleverness to solve. However, the sentence is describing an action, not a puzzle or a question posed to someone. So, "riddle" isn't the appropriate replacement for "paradox" in this context. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The revised sentence is: I played a prank on my sister by hiding fake spiders in her room.

In recent times, the Indian IPO market has experienced significant growth, driven by various Government of India (GOI) initiatives such as Make in India and Digital India, along with favourable regulations implemented by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). High foreign investment inflows and growing Private Equity (PE) and Venture Capital (VC) exits through IPOs, rather than the traditional mode of exits by selling stakes to other PE funds or through trade sales, have also contributed to this growth. As a result, many tech-led, Indian-founded but overseas-based startups are reverse-flipping to take advantage of the growing interest of both Indian and global investors in the Indian capital markets. Companies like PhonePe and Groww recently moved their headquarters to India, while others like Pine Labs and Flipkart are reportedly exploring similar options.

The Indian IPO market has seen strong demand for differentiated tech companies in recent years. As India's start-up ecosystem, particularly in sectors like enterprise tech, fintech, edtech, and e-commerce, matures, many companies have achieved unicorn status. The continued focus of GOI's Digital India initiative on building digital infrastructure is expected to further accelerate growth in this space, driving more tech IPOs. India's tech sector is experiencing an unprecedented boom, supported by these factors. This shift reflects a more discerning approach, influenced by tight monetary conditions, high inflation, market volatility, global economic slowdown, and increasing regulatory scrutiny. This focus on profitability has enhanced the IPO-readiness of startups, as public market investors typically seek more mature companies with proven revenue models and a clear path to operational profitability.

Biomimicry, the practice of drawing inspiration from nature to solve human challenges, is revolutionizing modern engineering. Nature, through millions of years of evolution, has perfected designs that are energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable. Engineers are increasingly looking to the natural world to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, whether in architecture, manufacturing, or materials science.

One of the most famous examples of biomimicry is the development of Velcro. The idea came from Swiss engineer George de Mestral, who observed how burrs stuck to his dog's fur. By mimicking the hook-and-loop mechanism of the burrs, Mestral created a fastening system that is now widely used. Another key example is the design of energy-efficient buildings inspired by termite mounds. Termites construct their nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain a stable temperature, even in extreme heat. Inspired by this, architects have designed climate-responsive buildings that reduce the need for artificial heating or cooling, saving energy.

In materials science, the lotus leaf's ability to resist dirt and water has led to the development of self-cleaning surfaces. These surfaces use microstructures similar to those on the leaf, preventing the accumulation of dust or grime. Similarly, researchers are studying the structure of spider silk, which is both incredibly strong and lightweight, to create synthetic materials for use in everything from medical sutures to aerospace components.

Biomimicry offers more than just clever designs. It emphasizes the importance of sustainability. By mimicking nature's solutions, engineers can create technologies that work in harmony with the environment, reducing waste and conserving resources. As this field continues to grow, it promises a future where human innovation is increasingly aligned with the natural world.

What is a key benefit of biomimicry as highlighted in the passage?

It encourages faster industrial production using synthetic chemicals.
It reduces the cost of manufacturing by using cheaper materials.
It promotes sustainable technologies that work in harmony with the environment.

Great-grandma is set to make hundred dolls for children who lost _____ in Beirut blast.
questions.solution_en:
'Theirs' is the correct possessive pronoun to be used because the sentence intends to convey that the great-grandma will make dolls for those children who lost their dolls in the blast. Possessive pronouns show that something belongs to someone. 'Theirs' is used to refer to the lost dolls of those children.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In China, there once lived a father, his four sons, and three daughters-in-law. His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village. Recently, these three new daughters-in-law had been brought into the house. Their new father-in-law's wife had died a few years before and having no mother-in-law with them in their new home, and being lonesome and homesick for their former families, they constantly asked the old man for permission to visit their former village. For you see, those were the days when young women, after they married and moved into the homes of their new husbands, needed permission to leave the household. Annoyed by the continual pleas of his three new daughters-in-law, the old father thought of a way to put an end to it.

He gave the young women permission in this way, saying, "You are always begging me to allow you to go and visit your mothers, and you think I am very hard-hearted for not letting you go. Now you may go, but only upon this condition. When you come back, you must each bring me something that I want. One of you must bring me some fire in paper, the other must bring me some wind in paper, and the third must bring me some music in wind. Unless you promise to bring me this, you are never to ask me to let you go home. And if you go and fail to get these for me, you are never to come back." The old man did not suppose that these conditions would be accepted. Of course, they were hard to understand, much less to fulfil. But the girls were young and thoughtless, and in their anxiety to get away did not consider any of that. So, they promised and made ready with speed. In great glee, they started off on foot to visit their mothers.

Why did the daughters-in-law leave in hurry as per the passage?
options_en: They were too concerned about the agreement between them and their father-in-law.
They were worried that their father-in-law would change his mind.
They were too eager to meet their mothers.
They didn't want to face their husbands.

questions.q_en: Describe how will you say The chef is preparing a delicious meal in the kitchen in passive voice.
options_en: A delicious meal is prepared in the kitchen by the chef.
A delicious meal is being prepared in the kitchen by the chef.
A delicious meal has been prepared in the kitchen by the chef.
A delicious meal was being prepared in the kitchen by the chef.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous tense. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous tense.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

By whom can the money be transferred to any account in India?
options_en: Whom can the money transfer to any account in India?
Who can transfer the money to any account in India?
Who could transfer the money to any account in India?
Who transfers the money to any account in India?
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option b).

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from passive to active. There is no change in the tense.

The following syntax is used for the above sentence:-

Passive voice- By whom + can + object + be + V3

Active voice- Who(subject) + can + V1 + object

Hence, the correct active voice form is “Who can transfer the money to any account in India?”
